heading: In 1968, California miner Joe Cullen found a 14.5-ounce gold nugget; 58 years later, the historic “Cullen Nugget” sold for $71,875
author: TOI World Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM /  Sep 21, 2026, 21:40 IST
paragraphs: California miner Joe Cullen found a substantial gold nugget at the Ruby Mine in Sierra County in 1968
Nearly six decades later, the 14.51-troy-ounce specimen known as the “Cullen Nugget” sold for $71,875 at Heritage Auctions' Nature and Science Signature Auction on April 29, 2026
The nugget weighs 451.41 grams and measures 2.44 by 2.24 by 0.77 inches
Heritage identifies it as native gold from the Ruby Mine on Mineral Mountain, part of the historic Alleghany Mining District, also known as the Forest Mining District
Its documented ownership history stretches from Cullen to W
Marshall Collection in 1993, before the specimen entered a private collection in the northeastern United States

Nearly 60 years after it was pulled from the California mine, the nugget returned to the auction market with its discovery and ownership history intact.Joe Cullen's 1968 discovery became a documented collector's specimenThe nugget's name comes directly from its original finder
Heritage describes the piece as the “Cullen Nugget”, named in honour of Joe Cullen, who collected it in 1968
Labels on the back of the specimen identify its association with the Ruby Mine in Sierra County
Marshall Collection, where it was catalogued in 1993 as #JHM4155, and finally a private Northeast Collection
That chain is significant for a mineral specimen because it connects the object being sold in 2026 with a specific discovery nearly 60 years earlier
Heritage describes the nugget as having a rounded, broad-disc form, a rich golden colour and a network of shallow cavities containing reddish-orange matrix
The auction house also notes its strong surface lustre and the natural shaping visible across the specimen
At 451.41 grams, the specimen weighs 14.51 troy ounces

Its relatively large surface area also gives the nugget a strong visual presence beyond its weight alone.The Ruby Mine sits in a historic California gold districtThe Ruby Mine lies in the Alleghany Mining District of Sierra County, a region with a long history of gold mining
Heritage describes the locality as a prolific gold-producing area that has been active since the 1850s, during the California Gold Rush
The district is also associated with the Forest Mining District name
The area became known for both lode and placer mining
Historical accounts of the Alleghany District identify the Ruby, Live Yankee and Bald Mountain drift mines among the major producers of the buried Tertiary gold channels
The Ruby Mine in particular produced coarse gold nuggets, with historical records noting that fist-sized nuggets were recovered there during the 1930s
The district is also home to the famous Sixteen-to-One Mine at Alleghany
The mine was incorporated in 1911 and became one of the best-known high-grade gold operations in the region

Records from the mine state that more than 1.1 million troy ounces of gold had been recovered from the Sixteen-to-One operation by 2011.The specimen's appearance reflects its natural historyUnlike a refined gold bar, a natural nugget retains the physical features created during its formation and subsequent movement through its environment
Heritage describes the Cullen Nugget as having a broad, rounded shape rather than a sharply defined crystalline form, with shallow cavities and areas of reddish-orange matrix across its surface
The auction house says those textures reflect both the nugget's primary formation and its later natural shaping
Its relatively large surface area also gives the specimen a strong visual presence beyond its weight alone
The dimensions help illustrate its unusual proportions
The nugget measures just over 6.2 centimetres long, 5.7 centimetres wide and 2 centimetres thick

At 451.41 grams, it is substantially heavier than an ordinary piece of jewellery-grade gold while retaining the irregular form of naturally occurring gold.The Cullen Nugget sold nearly 60 years after its discoveryHeritage offered the specimen as Lot 72086 in its April 29, 2026 Nature and Science Signature Auction
The auction record lists the final sale price at $71,875, with the winning bid coming from an internet bidder
The price places the Cullen Nugget among the notable gold specimens sold during that auction

Other gold pieces in the same sale included a 55.16-troy-ounce Australian nugget that sold for $262,500 and an 11.10-troy-ounce crystallised gold nugget from an unspecified locality that sold for $50,000
For the Cullen Nugget, however, its value as a collector's specimen rests on more than its weight
The piece carries a documented connection to a named miner, a specific California mine and a sequence of collections stretching back to its 1968 discovery
